newsitem.title: USA: El Paso, Texas, $14 mln bonds single-A - Fitch.
newsitem.headline: El Paso, Texas, $14 mln bonds single-A - Fitch.

text.p: The approximately $14.3M El Paso County Community College District (EPCC) combined fee revenue building and refunding bonds, series 1997, are assigned an underlying rating of 'A' by Fitch Investors Service.
The bonds are expected to be insured by AMBAC, whose claims-paying ability is rated 'AAA'.

The bonds are expected to be sold on or about Dec. 18 through negotiation by a syndicate led by BA Securities, Inc. Bond proceeds will be used to fund capital projects, refund approximately $1.0 million of outstanding bonds and pay issuance costs.
The capital projects include renovation of existing facilities and construction of a new campus, which will serve the Eastside/Lower Valley section of El Paso.

The 'A' rating is based on EPCC's strong support from state and local sources, as well as steadily increasing demand for its services. Approximately 44.1% and 24.7% of EPCC's revenue comes from state appropriations and local property taxes, respectively.

These two sources combined have provided a consistent level of support for the past five years, with state support generally decreasing and tax support increasing as a percentage of unrestricted revenue. Total full-time equivalent enrollment at its schools has increased to 14,229 in fall of 1996, from 11,994 in fall of 1992. This growth is fueled by an increasing need for basic educational and language skills, as the local population grows.

Highly competitive tuition rates should lead to continued success in attracting students; projected demographic trends are positive over the next 10 years. Risks include a relatively high debt load, inconsistent unrestricted operating margins and continued reductions in real growth of state appropriations.

These concerns are tempered by the flexibility afforded by low tuition rates and the growing need for the basic educational services provided by EPCC. Located in El Paso County, TX., EPCC was founded in 1969. It has grown to include three campuses (Valle Verde, Transmountain and Rio Grande), located in and around the City of El Paso, as well as several centers housing occupational and other training programs.

The planned opening of the new Eastside/Lower Valley facility will round out EPCC's presence in the community. Programs offered include transfer degree programs, vocational-technical career degrees (healthcare, hotel mgmt., computer programming, court reporting, among others), adult education, community service and developmental programs.
